title: Two sweeps, no move
prompt: It is 10:46 ET. Read the chart and decide.

intro.beginner: Price has taken a high and a low in the last hour. Ask what each of those moves did afterwards before you act on either.
intro.advanced: 10:46 ET. Both sides taken. What followed each?

whyNot.label: buying the sweep of the low
whyNot.why: It's the second sweep in 45 minutes and it didn't displace. The first one reversed straight back, so a long here is the same coin flip with the order reversed.

whyNot.label: selling the first sweep
whyNot.why: That one is over: it swept the high and drifted back, with no break of structure. It was never a signal, and the second sweep just showed it.

reference.summary: A range with both its high and its low taken inside an hour, and no displacement after either. A sweep is a reason to look; without displacement it's not a reason to act. No trade.

bias.why: The Daily and 4H are ranging; this morning is the same range.

decision.why: Two sweeps without displacement is chop. Nothing here has an edge.

take.why: A sweep without displacement isn't a setup.

draw.why: No clear draw: price took both sides and returned to the middle.

location.why: Price is back in the middle of the range.

annotations.label: Swept high 20,033.75
annotations.why: Took the range high and was back inside within minutes, with no break of structure after it.
annotations.whyNot: A sweep needs displacement behind it. This had none.

annotations.label: Swept low 19,968.75
annotations.why: The second sweep, same pattern: through the level, then a drift back.
annotations.whyNot: Two failed sweeps in a row is a market that's not moving.

annotations.label: Range high 20,020.25
annotations.why: The level that was swept, and nothing else came of it.

confluences.label: No displacement after either sweep
confluences.why: That's what makes them probes, not setups.

confluences.label: Price is back in the middle of the range
Sell-side liquidity just swept
confluences.why: True, and it didn't do anything.

lookFor: After a sweep, watch what happens next. Displacement and a break of structure make it a setup; a drift back makes it a probe.
Count the failed sweeps. Each one lowers the odds that the next is the real one.
A market that takes both sides and goes nowhere is telling you to wait.
